Ctrl+B on a US layout runs Bold.
Ctrl+Shift+B matches no binding: a binding's four modifiers must all equal the press's.
B without Ctrl types text, which reaches the engine as input.text, never as input.key.
Backspace is a document key.
Document keys match with any modifiers.
Tab moves focus out of the document in every shell.
Ctrl+C is the platform's copy, which the shell carries out.
Shift+Delete is the platform's cut on Windows and Linux, though Delete is a document key.
macOS has no Shift+Delete cut, so the document key Delete matches.
Alt with a letter belongs to the shell's KeyTips on Windows and Linux.
Ctrl+PageDown switches the browser's tab, though PageDown is a document key.
Natively, Ctrl+PageDown reaches the engine as the document key PageDown.
Alt+ArrowLeft is the browser's back on Windows and Linux.
On macOS, Alt+ArrowLeft is not kept, so it is the document key.
Ctrl with = is the browser's page zoom; no binding matches it either.
On macOS the manifest's Ctrl is Command.
On macOS, Ctrl+B is not Bold.
On iOS too, the manifest's Ctrl is Command.
Android keeps Ctrl.
ChromeOS keeps Ctrl.
An unknown platform counts as other, where Ctrl stays Ctrl.
On French AZERTY, Z is where US keyboards have W: Ctrl with the key that types z runs Undo.
On French AZERTY, the key in Z's US position types w: it does not run Undo.
AltGr+E types €; Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl and Alt together, which never falls back to the key's position.
On German QWERTZ, Z is where US keyboards have Y: Ctrl with the key that types z runs Undo.
On German QWERTZ, the key in Z's US position types y: Ctrl with it runs Redo.
AltGr+Q types @ on German keyboards.
On an Arabic layout, the key in B's position types لا: Ctrl with it runs Bold through its code.
On an Arabic layout, the key in Z's position types ئ: Ctrl with it runs Undo.
An Arabic letter without Ctrl types text.
On a Russian layout, the key in I's position types ш: Ctrl with it runs Italic.
On a Russian layout, Ctrl with the key in C's position types с, and is the platform's copy.
Ctrl+Shift+I opens the developer tools in a browser on Windows and Linux, also on a Russian layout.
Without a code that names a letter, a press that types another script matches nothing.
While an input method composes, it owns every key.
Enter commits the composition; the engine does not see it.
